# Introduction

A comb ledger records each frame of wax comb in a hive: when it was drawn, what it held, and when it was retired. Keepers who track comb age find that dark, old comb harbours more disease, so rotating frames on a schedule keeps a colony healthy.

## Why keep one

The ledger turns a vague sense of hive history into something a second keeper can read. Figure 1 shows a frame card pinned to the inside of the lid. Each card names the frame, the date it was drawn and the colony it came from.
